paras: The burning of a Black church and schoolhouse in De Soto County took place in late August 1905, when a masked band of "whitecappers" set fire to a "negro church and schoolhouse" and burned both to the ground. No one was identified, and the only known report is a short item in the Macon Beacon of Macon, Mississippi.

According to the Beacon, a band of whitecappers had recently been organized in De Soto county, and its "recent depredations" had caused "considerable excitement and indignation" there. The item does not name the state, though it ran among Mississippi news in a Mississippi weekly.
A few days before the report of 30 August 1905, the church and schoolhouse were burned to the ground by the band. The men were seen leaving the burning building, and all of them were masked.
The evidence left behind "gave no clue to the identity of the guilty parties," and no report of an arrest or investigation appears in the coverage.

The Beacon gave the burning a single unheadlined paragraph, placed between notice of a Confederate regimental reunion and a joke about an election. It described the band's acts as "depredations" and reported local indignation without further comment on the congregation or the school. No other white paper and no Black paper was found reporting the burning.
